question: Why did raising the P share from 0.4 to 0.6 at a P/Fe/Na ratio with Fe = 5 lengthen the defluidization time?
expect: premise false: 0.6/5/1 gave a SHORTER defluidization time than 0.4/5/1; high P weakened Fe's inhibitory effect (abstract; sec. 3.2)
rendered: According to the text, raising the P share from 0.4 to 0.6 at a P/Fe/Na ratio with Fe = 5 did not lengthen the defluidization time. Instead, it shortened the defluidization time. This is because high P concentrations weakened the inhibitory effect of Fe, leading to a shorter defluidization time for the P/Fe/Na ratio of 0.6/5/1 than for 0.4/5/1.
